item.title: U.S. Squeezes Cuba Even as It Searches for a New Regime Leader
item.description: Some officials warn that a more hard-line leader could emerge if the Trump administration moves forward with its plans.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Pager, Julian E. Barnes and Frances Robles
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Lisette Poole González for The New York Times
item.media:description: Cuba earlier this year. Many officials waiting in the wings in the country, like their Iranian counterparts, represent more hard-line factions.

item.title: Bill Cassidy Will Back Todd Blanche as Attorney General, Salvaging His Confirmation
item.description: The Louisiana senator said that, despite reservations, he would back President Trump’s pick for attorney general, giving Republicans enough votes for a majority.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold and Carl Hulse
item.media:description: Senator Bill Cassidy, Republican of Louisiana, said on Friday that he had come to believe that Todd Blanche would be better positioned to push back against President Trump’s demands than an alternative.

item.title: Trump Restarts Battle to Fire Sitting Fed Governor Lisa Cook
item.description: The Trump administration, rebuffed by the Supreme Court in its first attempt to fire Lisa D. Cook, sent the Federal Reserve governor a letter saying it was “considering” removing her from the job.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith and Maggie Haberman
item.media:description: Lisa D. Cook, a Federal Reserve governor, in Washington in January. President Trump this week renewed his threat to fire her.

item.title: Appeals Court Upholds Block on Trump Ballroom Construction
item.description: A federal appeals court panel backed a lower court’s ruling, and made it likely that the Supreme Court will decide the case. But the decision does not mean construction will halt immediately.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague and Mattathias Schwartz
item.category: White House East Wing and Ballroom (Washington, DC)
item.media:credit: Allison Robbert for The New York Times
item.media:description: Construction on the White House ballroom site this week.

item.title: Prosecutor Sues Justice Dept. Over Dismissal After Right-Wing Influencer’s Claim
item.description: Will Rosenzweig joins a growing list of former prosecutors and federal agents who have gone to court to contest the purge of law enforcement deemed disloyal.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer
item.media:description: The Justice Department in September fired Will Rosenzweig, a prosecutor who had earned consistent praise, hours after a right-wing commentator demanded on social media that officials dismiss him.

item.title: A Spurned Schumer Reaches Out to the Left
item.description: In a phone call this week, the Democratic leader told the new Michigan Senate nominee who had opposed him to just win, working to foster unity ahead of a difficult race.
item.dc:creator: Carl Hulse
item.media:description: Senator Chuck Schumer’s stewardship of Senate Democrats has stirred some grumbling from more progressive senators who resented his jumping into the primaries.

item.title: Max Miller Continues to Resist Pressure to Drop Out as Deadline Looms
item.description: The Republican House member from Ohio was accused of holding a gun to his ex-wife’s head and fracturing the collarbone of their young daughter. He has denied the accusations.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies and Annie Karni
item.media:description: Max Miller planned to loan his campaign $1 million, effectively rebuffing calls from powerful Republicans in the state to withdraw from the race.

item.title: They’re Battle-Tested Democrats. Do Voters Care?
item.description: Haley Stevens and Angie Craig were celebrated by Democrats in 2018. This year, they’ve faced tough primaries.
item.dc:creator: Jess Bidgood
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times; Nic Antaya for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representatives Angie Craig of Minnesota and Haley Stevens of Michigan

item.title: Iranians Say Trump’s Promises Have Fallen by the Wayside as Iran War Drags On
item.description: As President Trump struggles to extricate the United States from the war in Iran, his promises to protesters in the country have fallen by the wayside.
item.dc:creator: Erica L. Green, Zolan Kanno-Youngs, Sanam Mahoozi and Yeganeh Torbati
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Anti-government protesters in Tehran in January. Iran has executed at least 26 people in connection with the protests since President Trump made his promise.

item.title: Their African Islands Were Set to Be Decolonized. Then the U.S. Bombed Iran.
item.description: The inhabitants of the Chagos Islands were expelled by the British 60 years ago. Refugees were anxious to return this year, but their hopes have been caught in a morass of geopolitics.
item.dc:creator: John Eligon and Joao Silva
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
Destruction of Cultural Antiquities and Heritage
item.media:description: Roseline Rabouine, who was forced to leave Chagos Islands when she was 8, attending mass in Port Louis, Mauritius, last month.

item.title: Houthis Claim Attack on Yemeni Military Camp
item.description: Recent escalating tensions between the Iran-backed group and the Yemeni government have prompted fears that a truce in place since 2022 is nearing collapse.
item.dc:creator: Pranav Baskar and Shuaib Almosawa
item.media:description: Houthi supporters during a rally against the Saudi-led coalition in Sanaa, Yemen, last week.

item.title: She Is Russia’s Richest Woman. Her Business Empire Is Going Up in Flames.
item.description: As Ukraine repeatedly strikes warehouses of the e-commerce site Wildberries, Tatyana Kim, its billionaire co-founder, faces her biggest test yet.
item.dc:creator: Nataliya Vasilyeva, Paul Sonne, Alina Lobzina and Oleg Matsnev
item.media:description: Tatyana Kim, the billionaire co-founder of Wildberries, Russia’s largest online marketplace, in June.

item.title: What to Know About Wildberries, the Company in Ukraine’s Cross Hairs
item.description: Ukrainian drones have increasingly targeted warehouses belonging to Wildberries, which many Russians rely on as the country’s largest e-commerce business.
item.dc:creator: Nataliya Vasilyeva
item.media:description: An advertisement for Wildberries in Moscow. Several of the company’s warehouses have ceased operations after attacks from Ukraine.

item.title: Pellet Guns, Sticks and Tear Gas: How India’s Police Halted a Youth March
item.description: A New York Times analysis details the July 20 crackdown on unarmed protesters in New Delhi that has provoked public outrage and accusations of excessive force.
item.dc:creator: Anupreeta Das, Showkat Nanda and Jiawei Wang

item.title: Canada Offers U.S. Concessions in Trade Talks but Demands a Comprehensive Deal
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney is attempting to prevent 50 percent tariffs against many Canadian goods scheduled for this month.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: The American whiskey section at a B.C. Liquor Store, after U.S.-made products were removed from shelves in Vancouver last year.

item.description: What the former prime minister’s boyfriend rebrand says about the intersection of politics and entertainment.

item.title: Photos Show England Turning Brown in Drought
item.description: Beset by historically dry weather, much of the nation is losing its signature hue.
item.dc:creator: Kieran Corcoran
item.media:description: A parched park on the south bank of the River Thames in central London on Thursday, with Tower Bridge in the background.

item.title: New York City Hall Dismisses Haitian Workers After Loss of Protected Status
item.description: Officials said that dozens of Haitian workers for the city would lose their jobs, but warned that the number could easily reach the hundreds.
item.dc:creator: Emma Goldberg
item.media:description: City officials said dozens of city workers were affected, but that number could rise to the hundreds.

item.title: Mamdani Hosted a Town Hall About Buses. Why Was the D.S.A. There?
item.description: After Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s office invited the Democratic Socialists of America to a city-sponsored event, watchdog groups raised concerns about mixing politics with government work.
item.dc:creator: Dana Rubinstein and Stefanos Chen
item.media:credit: George Etheredge for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s office said the Democratic Socialists of America, a nonprofit 501(c)(4) organization that can participate in political activity, was invited to the event alongside other groups that work on transit issues.

item.title: Mamdani Faces Lawsuit Over Rollout of Second-Home Tax
item.description: Some New York City homeowners are arguing that they have been improperly targeted by the tax on high-end second homes, also known as pieds-à-terre.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Zaveri
item.media:description: A lawsuit filed by New York City homeowners does not seek to invalidate the tax on high-end second homes, but takes issue with the way it was introduced.

item.title: Reading Scores Drop for N.Y.C. Students Amid Revamp of Literacy Program
item.description: The declines nearly wiped out gains made in the state exams last year. New York City school leaders promised a review of the results.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Haag
item.media:description: Half of New York City’s public schoolchildren demonstrated proficiency on reading tests, a six-point drop from last school year.

item.title: Can Netflix Save a Summer Slump With a Stunt on Sunset Boulevard?
